events.title: The Poet Rumi Dies in Konya
events.description: Jalal al-Din Rumi, the Persian mystic and poet, died in Konya, in present-day Turkey. His followers gathered around his memory and later became known as the Mevlevi Order, or the 'whirling dervishes'.
events.significance: Rumi's poetry is among the most widely read in the world. His verse on love and spiritual longing still reaches audiences more than 750 years later.

events.title: Bolívar Declares the Independence of Gran Colombia
events.description: At Angostura, now Ciudad Bolívar in Venezuela, Simón Bolívar announced the creation of the Republic of Gran Colombia. It was meant to unite the territories of present-day Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador, and later Panama.
events.significance: The declaration was a major step in breaking Spanish rule in South America. It showed Bolívar's vision of a large, unified independent nation.

events.title: Simón Bolívar Dies
events.description: Simón Bolívar, the Liberator of much of South America, died at age 47 near Santa Marta in Colombia. He had resigned the presidency earlier in the year, and the union he built was falling apart.
events.significance: Bolívar is remembered as one of the central figures of Latin American independence. Several countries and a currency carry his name.

events.title: The Wright Brothers Make the First Powered Flight
events.description: Near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville and Wilbur Wright flew their Wright Flyer. They made several flights that morning. The first, piloted by Orville, lasted 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet.
events.significance: This was the first sustained, controlled flight of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft. It opened the age of aviation and changed travel, trade and warfare.
